questions.scenario_template: At fiscal year-end, the company records annual straight-line depreciation of ${amount_dollars} on factory equipment with an estimated useful life of 5 years and salvage value. Record the adjusting journal entry to recognize annual depreciation expense.

questions.scenario_template: For financial statement reporting under US GAAP, the company uses straight-line depreciation to reflect the steady economic consumption of its operating machinery, recording ${amount_dollars} of book depreciation expense for the year, while using accelerated MACRS on its tax return. Record the company's financial accounting adjusting entry for book depreciation.

questions.scenario_template: The company retires and sells factory equipment with an original cost of ${amount_dollars} and accumulated depreciation of 80% of original cost. The equipment is sold to an external buyer for cash proceeds equal to 25% of original cost, recognizing a gain on disposal. Record the derecognition of the asset and the sale transaction.

review.source: Stream-M06 Candidate Batch: UW Foster Module 6 PPE & Depreciation (Equipment Derecognition & Gain on Disposal)

questions.scenario_template: At year-end, the company performs an impairment review of production equipment under ASC 360 following technological changes. The equipment carrying value of $100,000 exceeds undiscounted expected future cash flows of $75,000 (triggering impairment under Step 1 recoverability). The fair value is measured at $60,000, requiring an impairment loss write-down of ${amount_dollars} (Step 2 measurement). Record the impairment loss adjusting entry.

review.source: Stream-M06 Candidate Batch: UW Foster Module 6 PPE & Depreciation (ASC 360 Two-Step Impairment Test)
